name: server-normal-v5
note: Protocol v5 (docs/NAVRH_PROTOKOL_V5.sk.md; package B4, lead's skeleton dokazy/B4/kostra/KOSTRA.md). Schema 3 is the v5 layout: scripts/protocol_v5.py reads every section; python3 scripts/collection.py --protocol config/collection-v5.json selfcheck checks the file and its plan. A value a later stage determines (proposal 10.9) is null or preliminary at its one place, and determined_at names the stage of each such path. The numbers of the G0 rows of proposal 10.9 are the author's proposal by judgment; the owner may change them before G1. The stage of this file is what the readiness records of scripts/gates.py say (gates.py status and require), not a field of the file: stage_binding hashes every value of the file at every stage, so a field that followed the stage would reopen the records of the stages before it; schema 3 therefore has no field status (question Q23), and schemas 1 and 2 keep theirs as history.
vms_note: The two lab VMs of config/collection-v4.json: one image (scripts/labctl.py clone from hyptcn-guest, Debian 12, kernel 6.1.0-42-cloud-amd64), every service deployed on both; the scenario decides the traffic only (proposal 5.2).

invalid_rows.note: Preliminary until G2 (POKYNY 2026-11-22 section 4): max 3 and the gate 557/720 above, bound by the inequality (ideal - 33 (max + 1)) / cycles < gate <= (ideal - 33 max) / cycles; G2 determines max by the formula of proposal 10.9 (at most 6) and the gate follows from it.

replacement.note: Proposal 7.5: the limit is the smallest number with a predicted probability of completing the plan of at least 0.95 at the rejection rate of the confirmatory rehearsal; null until G3b. A replacement keeps the VM, role, group, position, scenario and the event types or control kinds in order, and draws new times and a new traffic seed with its attempt number (proposal 7.3).

scenario_rule.basis: rate is the peak of the arrival envelope: the share peak_share of the server's throughput measured at saturation in G2 for the scenario's intensity; the mean follows from the envelope. The throughput (the lead's answer to Q5, 2026-11-24) comes from a diagnostic series per profile, no session, on a copy of this file whose max_concurrent does not bind (at least 4 x 60 x the highest rate of the series): a step fails on the server when a request of its peak lacks its expected result or the p95 latency of the peak is at least 1000 ms (the lab-test tool's judgment, scripts/lab_trial.py LATENCY_P95_BOUND_MS, no value of this file); a step with a user session dropped or without a peak is invalid (finding F1 of the B5c verification); after the first failed step the boundary is bisected (the lead's answer to Q5) at the geometric midpoint, rounded to three decimals (the executor's judgment, package B11), until the failed rate is less than 1.15 times the served one (the executor's reading, package B11, of the lead's "until neighbouring steps are closer than 15 %"); the throughput is the highest served rate.
scenario_rule.note: Peak shares 0.3 and 0.8 are the author's judgment (skeleton section 1); the peak-to-mean ratio of at least 2 is proposal 5.7 (author's proposal, judgment). The lab test on the VM after B5 checks the rule before G2 fixes rate. In G2 rate high must also hold the bounds of the cycle time (audit.cycle_ms_max) and the size of a session against the disk estimate of decision D12; if it does not, that is a finding for the lead, and peak_share 0.8 does not change by itself (the lead's answer to Q5, 2026-11-24). The order in G2: a cap that does not bind is set before the runs at rate high (profiles.*.max_concurrent is a value of G2), then the long runs at rate high, then twice their largest number of user sessions in progress.

arrivals.note: The envelope of the open loop (proposal 5.3, skeleton B5 section 2; scripts/host_traffic.py draw_envelope), drawn from the session's traffic seed over [0, dur]: a linear ramp from level 0 over [0, ramp_s], inside the warmup; one slow wave mean * (1 - amplitude * cos(2 pi (t - start) / period)) with the period in wave_period_s (20 to 40 minutes, skeleton section 2), the mean in wave_mean, the amplitude in wave_amplitude and the start of a cycle in [warmup, warmup + period); one short peak of level 1 lasting peak_s (2 to 4 minutes, skeleton section 2), a trapezoid whose two flanks take peak_edge_share of it each, inside [warmup, dur]. An envelope whose peak-to-mean over [warmup, dur] is below scenario_rule.min_peak_to_mean is drawn again. The envelope is piecewise linear with knots every step_s. ramp_s 120 is warmup_s; wave_mean, wave_amplitude, peak_edge_share and step_s are the author's judgment. peak_at uniform: the peak lies anywhere in [warmup, dur] (a sale).

client_errors.note: Deliberate client errors, share of all requests (proposal 5.3: 1 to 3 %; skeleton section 2: 2 %): after each request one follows with odds share / (1 - share), its status drawn from statuses: 400 a catalog page 0, 401 the cart with an invalid token, 404 the detail of a product beyond the catalog. The request log marks each with intended_status.

think_s.note: Before every request but the first of a user session: exponential with mean 7 s, cut at 70 s (proposal 5.7, TPC-W).

funnel.note: The funnel of skeleton section 2 (home, browse and search, detail, cart, order): home, then a number of catalog pages drawn uniformly from pages, each a search with search_share (a noun of the product names of lab/seed.py) or else a browse of a page drawn Zipf over the catalog pages of page_size products, each page followed by a number of product details drawn uniformly from details_per_page, each detail drawn Zipf over the products; after home, a page or a detail a static file follows with static_share, drawn Zipf over the static files of lab/seed.py. A user session orders with order_share of its intensity (proposal 5.7): a login (customer token), a number drawn uniformly from cart_items of the products it viewed into the cart, the cart, the order. Zipf has the exponent zipf_s (skeleton section 2). pages, search_share, details_per_page, static_share, cart_items and page_size are the author's judgment.

eshop.note: Profile eshop (proposal 5.2): customers' user sessions as a funnel against the catalog, the cart, the orders and the static files of the lab (lab/services.py, lab/nginx.conf; objects of lab/seed.py). order_share is proposal 5.7, zipf_s skeleton section 2. max_concurrent 500 is preliminary until G2 (determined_at G2; the lead's answer to Q5, 2026-11-24): G2 sets it to twice the largest number of user sessions in progress at rate high in its long run, after a cap that does not bind for that run; 500 is the author's judgment of the first value (a user session of about 9 requests lasts about a minute, so about 60 x rate are in progress at the peak), and the lab test on the VM measured that it binds at 8 user sessions per second. The saturation series of G2 runs on a copy whose max_concurrent is at least 4 x 60 x its highest rate (scenario_rule.basis).

arrivals.note: The envelope of the open loop (proposal 5.3, skeleton B5 section 2; scripts/host_traffic.py draw_envelope), drawn from the session's traffic seed over [0, dur]: a linear ramp from level 0 over [0, ramp_s], inside the warmup; one slow wave mean * (1 - amplitude * cos(2 pi (t - start) / period)) with the period in wave_period_s (20 to 40 minutes, skeleton section 2), the mean in wave_mean, the amplitude in wave_amplitude and the start of a cycle in [warmup, warmup + period); one short peak of level 1 lasting peak_s (2 to 4 minutes, skeleton section 2), a trapezoid whose two flanks take peak_edge_share of it each, inside [warmup, dur]. An envelope whose peak-to-mean over [warmup, dur] is below scenario_rule.min_peak_to_mean is drawn again. The envelope is piecewise linear with knots every step_s. ramp_s 120 is warmup_s; wave_mean, wave_amplitude, peak_edge_share and step_s are the author's judgment. peak_at wave_start: the peak begins where a cycle of the slow wave begins (its lowest level), the login wave at the beginning of the slow wave (skeleton section 2): every corp user session begins with a login.

client_errors.note: Deliberate client errors as in eshop (proposal 5.3, skeleton section 2), in the forms of corp: 400 a document list page 0, 401 a login with a wrong password, 404 a document id that never exists.

think_s.note: Exponential with mean 10 s, cut at 100 s, the author's judgment: an employee reads a document longer than a customer a page (proposal 5.7 fixes the think time of eshop only).

document_sizes.note: Upload sizes, lognormal with a Pareto tail (skeleton section 2): with tail_share a Pareto size from tail_from_bytes with index tail_alpha, else lognormal with the median median_bytes and sigma; cut to [min_bytes, max_bytes], max_bytes the 8 MiB cap of the docs service (lab/services.py MAX_DOCUMENT). The numbers are those of the seeded documents (lab/seed.py document_size, the B5a executor's judgment).

corp.note: Profile corp (proposal 5.2): an employee logs in with a password (lab/seed.py employee_password), then takes a number of document actions drawn uniformly from actions, each drawn by shares: a document list page (drawn Zipf over the pages of page_size documents), a download (drawn Zipf over the seeded documents), an upload (document_sizes) or a report request, which the worker runs as three subprocesses and whose status the employee checks once. Zipf has the exponent zipf_s. The login wave is arrivals.peak_at wave_start. actions, shares, page_size and zipf_s are the author's judgment. max_concurrent 250 is preliminary until G2 (determined_at G2; the lead's answer to Q5, 2026-11-24): G2 sets it to twice the largest number of user sessions in progress at rate high in its long run, after a cap that does not bind for that run; 250 is the author's judgment of the first value, and the lab test on the VM measured that it binds at 8 user sessions per second. The saturation series of G2 runs on a copy whose max_concurrent is at least 4 x 60 x its highest rate (scenario_rule.basis).

events.note: Five types and the empty event (decision D8). A session has no event or three; exactly one session of every group has none (proposal 5.5, 7.2). Durations are drawn continuously in duration_s; the free time of the session is split at random over all gaps. first_s 300, min_gap_s 480, tail_s 360 and grace_s 60 are the author's judgment (skeleton section 4): the gap is the reverberation of 300 s plus one full window of 160 s and a reserve, the tail the reverberation and the fading of the stop, the start the first window and two minutes of scored clean traffic. min_per_type is the table of proposal 7.2 (judgment by proposal 10.9).

full_snapshot_guard.note: Proposal 5.5: no event and no control starts from before_s before a full snapshot to the first scored row after it, that is the full snapshot's row + window_rows (judgment by proposal 10.9).

kontrola_wx_memfd.note: Skeleton B8 section 1: one process with a touched W+X page and an open memfd (the pilot's positive control of protocol v4); its paired negative is the same program with the page RW and a file in /tmp instead of the memfd. The occurrence adds one process with each pattern; the expected shift of each column is half of that, 0.5, which tells one more from none (judgment; a value of G0, controls.note).

kontrola_modul_jadra.note: Skeleton B8 section 1: modprobe of the first candidate present in the guest kernel's package, not loaded and without dependent modules, none of which creates a device or a network interface (lab/udalosti.py MODULE_CANDIDATES holds the same names); its paired negative runs modprobe -n of it; the stop is modprobe -r. The candidates are the lead's judgment until the lab test on the VM confirms them (skeleton section 6). The occurrence adds one module; the expected shift of mod_total is half of it, 0.5 (judgment; a value of G0, controls.note). mod_delta is no column: the load falls into the row of the start, so every row wholly inside the occurrence has 0 (design B8, addendum).

kontrola_pocuvajuci_soket.note: Skeleton B8 section 1: a process listens on a TCP port outside the ports of the lab (lab/udalosti.py CONTROL_PORT, loopback); its paired negative is the same process with the socket bound and not listening. The occurrence adds one listening socket; the expected shift of sock_listen is half of it, 0.5 (judgment; a value of G0, controls.note).

kontrola_zapisovac_pamate.note: Skeleton B8 section 1: a process holds N MiB, the dose (16, 64 or 256 MiB), and rewrites them with random bytes once per collection interval; its paired negative is the same process that writes them once and then waits. 2, 2 and 3 occurrences per dose among the kind's controls and the same among its negatives (per_dose); the doses and the counts are the lead's judgment. The lowest dose is chosen so that it is expected not to be caught (proposal 7.4, last paragraph; skeleton B8 section 1), and the protocol says so here, before any data. The expected shifts per dose are judgment and values of G0 (controls.note): of mem_changed_ratio half of the dose's share of the guest's 2048 MiB (every row of the control sees the dose changed again), of mem_changed_max and of mem_entropy_mean (bits per byte; random bytes have the highest entropy) the author's guess of how the writer's pages fill the bins and outweigh the other changed pages.

kontrola_davka_procesov.note: Skeleton B8 section 1: a parent starts K short processes a second, the dose (2, 10 or 50 a second); its paired negative is the same parent with one long child. 2, 2 and 3 occurrences per dose among the kind's controls and the same among its negatives (per_dose); the doses and the counts are the lead's judgment. The lowest dose is chosen so that it is expected not to be caught (proposal 7.4, last paragraph; skeleton B8 section 1), and the protocol says so here, before any data. The expected shifts per dose are judgment and values of G0 (controls.note): a short process lives 2 s (lab/udalosti.py BATCH_CHILD_S), so every row of the control sees about 2K processes the row before did not and misses about 2K of its own; the expected shift of proc_new and of proc_gone is half of that, K; of proc_total K + 2, about half way between the negative's three processes and the control's 2K children with its two.

controls.note: Controls on the VM, classes A (edge) and B (volume), proposal 7.4: 7 controls and 7 paired negatives per kind, at least 60 s each, horizon 180 s from the start (skeleton B8 section 1, the lead's number), only in role test_controls with three slots per session; 70 controls fill 70 of the 72 slots and the plan records the two empty ones (skeleton section 6). Durations as the events (B8 skeleton). Package B8: every kind states its class, its doses and its occurrences per dose (per_dose; null for class A, which has no dose), the feature columns it should move (features/snapshot.py MENA) with the expected shift of each over the occurrence against the mean of the 12 rows before its start (skeleton section 4; a number, or for class B one per dose), and the module kind its candidates. baseline is the tolerance of the level part of the return predicate (skeleton section 3): null until G2, then for processes and MemAvailable_kb the band [low, high] of their change since the start of the session, the 1st to the 99th percentile in a long lab trial without events. The numbers are the author's judgment by proposal 10.9. The expected shifts (controls.kinds.*.expect) are values of G0 (the lead's answer to question Q20, 2026-11-24; finding S6 of the B8 verification): judgment by proposal 10.9, which the owner may change only before G1, and not in determined_at; G2 checks them on the lab with controls.baseline, and a kind that misses its expected shift is a finding for the lead and a change of the protocol before G3, not a new value set in silence.

streams.rule: seed = int(sha256(json.dumps([name, group, session, attempt, purpose])).hexdigest()[:16], 16) with the protocol name (the rehearsal's own name in rehearsal mode); session-level purposes (event_times, traffic, traffic_arrivals, traffic_choices, traffic_sizes) take the group name, the position and the attempt; role-level ones (event_free_position, event_deck, control_deck, phase_deck) the role name as group, session -1 and attempt 0; scenario_order is drawn per block of len(scenarios) groups of a role, with group <role>/<block>, session -1 and attempt 0; the purposes of the analysis (package B7a), which the plan does not draw, take session -1 and attempt 0 as well and as group: z0_alarms the role on whose windows the random variant of Z0 places its alarms, bootstrap the comparison <claim>/<method> of a confirmatory claim with one method it compares (for example k1/Z3); the analysis draws from numpy.random.default_rng(seed), z0_alarms the repetitions of the random variant of Z0 in order, each one number of [0, 1) for every window of the role in the order of its window set (tcn/metody.py Z0_RANDOM_RULE), bootstrap the resamples of the interval first and then, above analysis.statistics.exact_up_to_boots boots, the sign vectors of the test (scripts/protocol_v5.py analysis_seed); injections (package B7b), which the plan does not draw either, takes session -1 and attempt 0 and as group the carrier role and the class <role>/<class> of the interventions of K2 (test_benign/C, test_benign/D, test_controls/C, test_controls/D) or dev for the interventions inserted into dev for the selection of Z1, and the analysis draws the placements of each unit from numpy.random.default_rng(seed) in the order tcn/zasahy.py UNIT_RULE states (for dev C first, then D; per class the deal of the lengths, then of the orders or groups, then per intervention its start, its donor for D and its permutation for C in random order)
streams.note: Every purpose has its own random stream (proposal 5.5); the seeds are new, the v4 schedule was looked at during the fault analysis (proposal 7.3). The traffic of a session (package B5b, skeleton B5 section 2): traffic draws the arrival envelope and is the session's seed, traffic_arrivals the arrival times, traffic_choices the choices of every user session and traffic_sizes the upload sizes (scripts/host_traffic.py). Package B7a adds the streams of the analysis z0_alarms and bootstrap (design B7a 1.6); the plan draws neither, and every purpose has its own seed, so no seed of the plan changed. Package B7b adds the stream injections of the interventions into features (design B7b 1.4); the plan draws it neither, so no seed of the plan changed. The fix of package B9a removed the stream guest_reset of B9a, one seed per group: every group of both modes starts from the one seeded level seeded_level, a value of the protocol and no random stream (proposal 5.4, chapter 12, question Q18 to the lead); the plan never drew it, so no seed of the plan changed.

seeded_level.note: The seed of lab/guest_state.py reset --seed at the start of every group of both modes (scripts/protocol_v5.py reset_seed). Proposal 5.4: every group starts with a new QEMU process and the database restored to its seeded level; the table of chapter 12 decides 'stav databázy na začiatku skupiny | pevný seedovaný stav' against the drift of the inputs (chapter 2.2). Question Q18, accepted by the lead 2026-11-24: one level for every group of both modes, the level lab/install.sh seeds (python3 guest_state.py reset --seed 0), so seed 0. The campaign checks that the guest echoes it. lab/guest_state.py reset takes 1 to 18 digits, so the seed is an integer of 0 to 10^18 - 1. It lies in the streams section so that every protocol that takes that section of this file has it.

periodicity.note: author's judgment in G0 (proposal 10.9), not a mechanism; the spacings are those between the starts of bursts of flagged rows (lead's remarks on B3, part 2)

audit.collector_majflt_note: The bound of the collector's major faults per cycle (the lead's answer to question Q29, 2026-11-24; risk capture R4 of the code audit data/results/audit_kodu_v5_20261120.json, whose protocol control asked for collector majflt 0). The count is capture.rusage.majflt of every sidecar, the major faults of the collector's sampling thread during that cycle (getrusage RUSAGE_THREAD, vmicollect/src/collector.c). The audit of every session of schema 3 records and prints the largest count of one cycle, its seq, the sum and the cycles counted (scripts/collection.py majflt_record, values.collector_majflt); a sidecar whose count is missing or no integer of at least 0 is a reason, never 0. collector_majflt_max is null until G2 (determined_at, proposal 10.9): until then the counts are recorded and printed and never a reason. The rule, written before the data: the largest count per cycle observed in the error-free runs of G2 on both VMs; at zero the bound is 0. From G2 on the audit rejects a session with a cycle above the bound, and the audit self-test builds the case of one cycle at the bound + 1 (scripts/tests/audit_cases.py cases).

early_stop.note: The early stop of a campaign (proposal 7.5 and 10.9; the lead's skeleton B9 row skoré zastavenie, package B9b and its fix, question Q24): after every audit the campaign stops when the session was rejected for periodicity (periodicity_stops; one session suffices, the lead's judgment in the skeleton's section 5) or when the campaign's count of marked rows at an event type is above its bound. The marked rows are the invalid rows and the rows a parser rule closed (as features/acceptance.py marks them) whose time lies in the event window of an occurrence of that type, the window of the session's log audit (features/acceptance.py MARKED_ROWS_RULE). The count C_T sums them, and n_T the occurrences of the type, over the audited sessions of both VMs since the count's restart point (the start of the campaign, or its latest recorded ending with an early-stop trigger, which a written analysis answers before the campaign runs again; a continuation counts on from the paused campaign it continues until its own first ending with an early-stop trigger: the accepted text of Q24, 's náhradami aj s pokračovaním'; question Q24 accepted by the lead 2026-11-24, package B11). The bound is the 99th percentile of the Poisson distribution at rate_T x n_T, rate_T the rate of marked rows per occurrence in marked_rows_rate_per_type, determined at G3b from G2 and G3b together (proposal 10.9); null until then, so the count is printed in the runner's state and stops nothing (features/audit_policy.py EARLY_STOP_RULE, with the false-stop rates of the executor's Poisson model, a model and not a measurement).

background.note: Background activity of corp (proposal 5.7: the author's proposal without a direct source): outside every event window at least one successful login and one accepted report request, and the largest document download at least 10 times the median one (a long tail of sizes); the three numbers are the author's judgment (package B5b).

traffic.note: The bounds of the realism requirements (scripts/traffic_log.py realism) and of the offered-load check, G0 by proposal 10.9. Proposal 5.3: the offered load outside event windows within 20 % of the plan. Proposal 5.7: arrival spacings with a coefficient of variation of 0.8 to 1.2, computed on spacings rescaled by the planned envelope (skeleton B5 section 4); the most requested tenth of the objects gets at least half of the requests; at least 88 % and less than 100 % successful answers outside events; response sizes over at least two orders of magnitude. The think-time mean and the order share may differ from the profile's design value (profiles, proposal 5.7) by at most 4 standard errors of their sample (the sample standard deviation over the square root of the count; for the order share sqrt(p (1 - p) / n) of the design share p): a two-sided test whose false refusal is about 6e-5 per session under the normal approximation, the author's judgment (package B5b). The peak-to-mean bound is scenario_rule.min_peak_to_mean. The think-time maximum is judged on the realized think times (from the end of a request to the start of the next request of its user session) and may lie at most 1 s above profiles.eshop.think_s.max, the generator's own delay (scripts/traffic_log.py THINK_LAG_S, the executor's judgment, package B10, finding F6 of the B5b verification). D_max of the order share, order_share_session_max_s (package B13, the lead's answer to Q73 point 1, 2026-11-25): a user session is left out of the order share when it starts in [window start - D_max, window end] of an event window, by its start alone, whatever its later requests touch, since a selection by overlap with a window depends on the length of a user session and an ordering one is longer (the C4 pass, dokazy/G1/kod/vysledok_C3b.json: of its 16 sessions with three events the share lay below the design value in 15 and at it in one). One constant for every kind of user session: 242 s, the duration that an ordering user session of profiles.eshop, the longest kind, exceeds with probability 0.001 (241.68 s, rounded up to whole seconds), computed exactly from the profile: its N - 1 think times exponential with the mean think_s.mean, N its requests as the funnel and the deliberate client errors draw them (scripts/host_traffic.py Eshop); the cut at think_s.max, which only shortens, and the requests' own duration (milliseconds on the lab, 0 s in the dry run) are left out. The level 0.001 is the executor's judgment (package B13); scripts/tests/test_traffic_realism.py recomputes the value from the profile.

invalid_rows.cause: rows invalid only because a named traversal did not close
invalid_rows.decision: invalid_rows rule of the protocol (owner 2026-11-17): at most max such rows, never scored

rule_closed_rows.cause: process lists a parser rule closed (prev, tail, meet)
rule_closed_rows.decision: complete lists, only reported; rule_closed_rows_max caps them from G3b

unconfirmed_findings.cause: cross-view differences seen in one snapshot only
unconfirmed_findings.decision: a difference of the live read is a finding once the next snapshot confirms it

inconclusive_integrity.cause: integrity checks that could not conclude
inconclusive_integrity.decision: integrity availability is no behaviour input (features/quality.py)

collector_warnings.cause: collector warnings that match an allowed pattern
collector_warnings.decision: audit.warnings_allowed, determined in G2; null allows none

event_traffic_exit.cause: traffic generator exit code 1 in an event session
event_traffic_exit.decision: failed requests inside an event window are evidence of the event

event_unit_restarts.cause: units an event type restarts by design (EVENT_UNITS)
event_unit_restarts.decision: any other restart stays a problem

event_window_requests.decision: inside [host start - 1 s, host stop done + grace] failures are expected

event_window_health_checks.cause: health polls without request id inside a window
event_window_health_checks.decision: lab/udalosti.py polls health without a request id, inside an event window and inside the start and stop calls of a control (package B8)

event_window_journal.cause: tracebacks and worker errors inside a window
event_window_journal.decision: outside every window they reject the session

event_window_nginx_errors.cause: nginx error lines inside a window
event_window_nginx_errors.decision: outside every window they reject the session

architecture.note: The TCN of the thesis on the collection window (proposal 10.1 point 3): kernel 3, four blocks of 16 channels, dropout 0.1, no weight normalization (SULAD_S_TEXTOM_PRACE table 1, row TCN; safeguard/model.py architecture() at 32 rows), a receptive field of 61 rows (tcn/model.py). learning_rate 0.001, gradient_clip 5 (the norm of one clip_grad_norm_ of the predictor) and batch_size 32 are today's constants of safeguard/training.py, and classifier_gradient_clip 5 is the classifier head's own clipping norm (proposal 8.2: the head is separated from the predictor's training), the same number (judgment). The training of package B6b reads every key.

stopping.note: Proposal 8.3: when the selected epoch is the last one, training is repeated once with twice the cap. Patience 10 and the cap of 100 epochs are the author's judgment.

Z0.what: never alarms; random alarms at the matched alarm rate

Z1.what: a threshold per column on its value, first difference, rolling mean and CUSUM; also a threshold on mem_changed_max

Z2.what: some count differs from its mode

Z3.what: prediction by the last value, the window mean and EWMA, with the EWMA coefficient as its free parameter (skeleton B7 section 2)

Z4.what: a threshold on the offered load (variant load); the residual of a regression of the features on the load (variant residual); each variant is a comparison of its own in K2a, and 'better' needs M to beat both (the lead's answer to question Q13, 2026-11-24)

Z5.what: linear autoregression (ridge) on the same window

M.what: the TCN of architecture, seeds 0 to 4

analysis.selection: One procedure on dev for every method with free parameters, never on a test role (the lead's skeleton dokazy/B7/kostra/KOSTRA.md section 2): Z1 by the share of the interventions inserted into dev that it detects at the matched alarm rate (package B7b), Z3 and Z5 by their prediction loss on dev, M by the rule of analysis.stopping (the epoch of the best dev loss, package B6); Z0, Z2 and Z4 have no free parameter (grid {}). Ties go to the first grid point (author's judgment, proposal 8.3).

zscore.what: z-score: the mean over the inputs of the squared z-score of the window mean, its mean and deviation fitted on train (tcn/baselines.py ZScoreAnomalia)
zscore.note: It draws nothing: seeds null, and it runs once with seed None (scripts/protocol_v5.py UNSEEDED; an empty list would mean that it never runs; the executor's convention of the merge of B7a).

iforest.what: isolation forest over the flattened window, fitted on train (tcn/baselines.py IsolationForestAnomalia)
iforest.note: Its subsamples and splits are random: it runs on every seed of analysis.seeds and every seed is reported, as for M (judgment).

gru.what: GRU predictor of the window's last row from the rows before it, with the loss of the TCN and a parameter count close to the TCN of analysis.architecture (tcn/baselines.py GRUPrediktor, skryte_pre_prediktor)
gru.note: Seeds 0 to 4 and a parameter count close to the TCN: the lead's addendum 2 point 1 of skeleton B7.

lstm.note: Seeds 0 to 4 and a parameter count close to the TCN: the lead's addendum 2 point 1 of skeleton B7.

matched_rate.budget: median over the seeds of M's alarms on the clean traffic of calibration, rounded up
matched_rate.note: Proposal 8.3 and the lead's skeleton B7 section 3: every method gets the same windows, M's normalizer and the rule k of n (analysis.alarm_rule), and an alarm is a rising edge of that rule. The budget is the count of M's alarms on the clean traffic of role calibration (its scored windows outside the events and their reverberation reverberation_s, proposal 4.2; the lead's answer to question Q12, 2026-11-24: the full-snapshot band is no part of clean traffic and bounds only where the interventions are placed; the controls of test_controls with their reverberation are no clean traffic either, judgment as tcn/metody.py CLEAN_RULE), the median over analysis.seeds rounded up. The threshold of a method walks its observed scores from the top down and takes the last one before the first at which its alarm count exceeds the budget (the count is not monotonic in the threshold); with a budget of 0 that is the most sensitive threshold without an alarm (the lead's judgment). In K2 each seed of M walks to the budget like every method (tcn/k2.py DETECTION_RULE; judgment: M enters K2 by the median of the shares of its seeds, so each seed is held to the alarm budget of its comparators), and the diagnostics of the alarm rule and of the threshold from clean traffic report each seed so beside its bundle threshold (tcn/diagnostiky.py SEED_WALK_RULE; verification of B7b, F4). The actual rate on test_benign is reported for every method in alarms per observed hour of clean traffic (its rows outside the events and their reverberation times interval_s, proposal 8.3 and 4.2), with the scored share of that time and the alarms per scored clean hour beside it. Z0 never alarms; its random variant alarms at the matched rate, z0_repetitions repetitions from the stream z0_alarms, and the mean is reported (200, the lead's number).

qualification.note: Proposal 8.1 and the lead's skeleton dokazy/B6/kostra/KOSTRA.md section 3, with the lead's answers of 2026-11-24 to questions Q7, Q8 and Q25 (package B11); features/qualification.py applies them and proposes analysis.columns. The rows are those of the roles of the plan mode, the same for every check (the executor's reading of Q7): in G3a every role of the rehearsal (30 sessions; in a rehearsal nothing is sealed), on the repetition on the campaign train and dev; in a session of test_controls the rows of every control and of its paired negative are left out, from host_start_unix to max(host_stop_unix, host_start_unix + controls.horizon_s), and the rows of the events stay (Q25; the record states the rows left out per session). near_constant_share 0.01 (a column with fewer than 1 % of its rows off the mode is near-constant, the rule channel) and identity_auc 0.75 (a column fails when max(AUC, 1 - AUC) of its value alone exceeds it when VM a is told from VM b, the first half of the session order from the second, or one group with all its sessions from the other groups, over all sessions, after the additive effect of scenario and position, fitted by least squares on the session means, is subtracted from every row; no strata, the lead's change of Q7 after finding F2 of the verification of B6a: a systematic shift between VMs or in time carries over from training to test as an error, while a random level of one session is ordinary variability, which the predictor sees in the window's context) are the lead's judgment (skeleton section 3, proposal 10.9). The adjusted values are rounded to 1e-6 x analysis.scale.floor of the column, so that the float residue of the fit breaks no exact tie, and of equal scores the worst comparison named is the first in the order vm, order, then the groups by name (both judgment, package B11). A failing level column is judged again by its first difference by the whole qualification: rule_differenced when that is constant or near-constant (the rule channel judges the column's change since the session's first measured row; Q8, accepted by the lead 2026-11-24), else differenced or dropped by the identity test of the first difference; any other failing column is dropped. duplicate_tolerance 1e-9 is the smallest singular value over the largest at or below which the rank test of the standardized columns takes a column for an exact linear combination of those kept before it (judgment: the float64 round-off of that test is of order rows x 2.2e-16, 2.2e-11 at 1e5 rows, while a column one unit off an exact combination in one row of 1e6 leaves about 1e-3, so 1e-9 lies orders of magnitude from both). level_columns are the columns that state the level of a state rather than the change in one interval, replaced by their first difference when they fail the identity test (judgment from their definitions in features/snapshot.py): the counts of processes, modules, sockets and processes with W+X or memfd pages, and mem_zero_ratio, the share of zero pages of the whole memory (the collector counts them over every page it reads, vmicollect/src/perbin.c and writer_delta.c; proposal 2.2 calls it a level column; accepted by the lead 2026-11-24 in his answer to Q7); proc_new, proc_gone, mod_delta and the other memory columns are changes within the interval.

scale.note: Proposal 8.2 and the lead's skeleton dokazy/B6/kostra/KOSTRA.md section 2: per_bin (every bin that enters the score has a scale of its own) and min_bin_pages 1024 (a bin of fewer pages never enters the score) are the lead's judgment (proposal 10.9). The same bins give the eight global memory columns, mem_bins_active included (Q10, 2026-11-24: the lead's answer to question Q10, finding F4 of the B6b verification): the extractor computes them only from the bins of at least min_bin_pages pages (features/snapshot.py counted_bin, also the predicate of the normalizer's NormalizationRule.split_bins), the audit with this min_bin_pages and the live run with its bundle's, so one changed page of a bin of one page never gives mem_changed_max 1.0, and a snapshot without such a bin is an extraction error. floor is the lower bound of each column's scale in the neural channel, the smallest change the quantity can show, so that a column just above near-constant gets no huge weight (proposal 8.2): 1 for every count (skeleton section 2), and for the other columns the step of the quantity by its definition (judgment, skeleton section 7) over those bins (Q10, 2026-11-24): mem_changed_ratio and mem_zero_ratio one page of the 524288 pages of the bins of at least min_bin_pages pages of the hyptcn-lab layout (128 bins of 4096 pages; its bins of 1 and of 64 pages are left out; data/results/collection_pilot_7_20261026_audit.json values.layout), mem_bins_active one of those 128 bins, mem_changed_max and mem_changed_p95 one page of a full bin (bin_bytes of 4 KiB pages, 4096), mem_entropy_mean and mem_entropy_max the collector's print resolution of a bin's entropy_mean (6 decimals, vmicollect/src/meta.c), and mem_changed_spread, a normalized entropy of integer page counts with no step of its own, the same 1e-6. local_floor is the same rule for the scaled values of a bin (has_changed is a mask): changed_ratio and zero_ratio one page of a full bin, entropy_mean 1e-6. The floors of the memory columns assume that layout on both VMs; a corpus holds one layout (features/dataset.py), G3a records it.

k2a.statistic: D = share of detected interventions of M minus that of Z per boot

k2b.statistic: D = share of detected interventions of M minus that of Z per boot

statistics.note: Proposal 8.4 and 9.1, the lead's skeleton B7 section 4: per claim and compared method the values per boot (K1: I, K2: D). The interval is the percentile bootstrap over the boots at level 0.95 (chapter 8.4: the interval is 95 % of the values per boot): bootstrap resamples of the boots with replacement, the statistic of each its mean over the boots (judgment), the bounds the quantiles (1 - level)/2 and (1 + level)/2 of those means (numpy, linear). The test is the two-sided sign-flip permutation test of the values minus m over the boots (two-sided as chapter 9.2 counts it: 4 boots cannot give p below 0.125, 8 boots 0.008), its statistic the sum of those differences, computed exactly: by full enumeration of the 2^n sign vectors up to exact_up_to_boots boots, else of bootstrap random sign vectors with p = (1 + count) / (1 + bootstrap) (judgment). Both come from the stream bootstrap of the comparison (streams.rule). The interval decides the outcome, the p-value is reported; fewer than 2 boots are refused (judgment: one boot has no spread). bootstrap 10000 and exact_up_to_boots 16 are the lead's judgment.

validity.note: Proposal 7.4 and the lead's answer to question Q14 (2026-11-24: a new deviation, valid from G1 on and never tuned), computed from the features alone (tcn/zasahy.py VALIDITY_RULE). An intervention is invalid when after it some value of the block or of its edges lies outside the quantiles of the same quantity at the last rows of the windows of role train (numpy, linear) and also outside the range the same quantity of the same input had at the same rows before the intervention (judgment: that range is its minimum to its maximum over those rows of the session). The quantities: every TCN input column (its value as M's normalizer gives it, a column of class differenced by its first difference), its first difference (the row minus the row before it) and its moving average (the mean of the last moving_average_rows rows, taken over the sorted rows of the window, in train and in the copies alike: judgment, so that a permutation of the rows of a window keeps its mean bit for bit). The rows: from the block's first row to the last row whose moving average reads a row of the block, the first difference back after the block among them. Every value at those rows is judged, not only the changed ones; a value the intervention leaves in place lies in its own range and never fails. The values of the scored bins are not judged (judgment, as before question Q14: a column is a TCN input column; at these quantiles a bin that changes in fewer than 0.1 % of the train rows has lo = hi). G3a reports the share of the volume class by class and length (tcn/k2.py VOLUME_FINDING_RULE: volume_share in the table of K2 and volume_finding); a share above one half at some length is a finding for the lead, never a change of this predicate. The quantiles 0.001 and 0.999 are the lead's judgment; moving_average_rows 6 (30 s) is the author's judgment: the shortest block, so that the average at the last row of a block of any length reads block rows only and shows a level shift of the block in full.

interventions.volume_class: An intervention whose copy fails the validity predicate goes to the volume class (proposal 7.4: it is moved, never dropped; the lead's skeleton B7 section 5: reported apart). It is not evaluable: it counts as detected by no method in the share of its planned class (the table by class and length) and in the pooled share of K2 (interventions.note), whose denominators stay the planned interventions (proposal 6.4), and the volume class is reported in a table of its own by planned class and length with the share each method detects (judgment).
interventions.note: Proposal 7.4 and the lead's skeleton B7 sections 5 and 9 (design B7b 1.2): C reverses or shuffles the rows of a block (orders), D replaces one group of columns in a block by the same rows of another session of the same scenario and position (groups); the lengths of 6, 12, 24 and 48 rows and six interventions of each class per boot in the 20 boots of test_benign and test_controls are the lead's numbers. Each intervention lies on a copy of one session of its own (the rows outside its block stay bit for bit), in placeable traffic (tcn/metody.py PLACEABLE_RULE: clean scored traffic outside the events, the controls, their reverberation and the full-snapshot band), and changes only the inputs of the neural channel (the TCN inputs and the scored bins of M's normalizer). Within a role the lengths differ by at most 1 (the lead's rule), and so do the orders of C and the groups of D (judgment); the placements come from the unit <role>/<class> of the stream injections. The same plan per boot of dev, from the unit dev of the stream, gives the interventions inserted into dev: they select Z1 (analysis.selection) and never enter K2. The groups of D are judgment from the definitions in features/snapshot.py: memory holds the eight aggregates mem_* and the four channels of every scored bin, from whose page counts the aggregates are computed (the has_changed of a bin masks its entropy, so a bin stays whole); processes the counts of processes, of the new and the gone ones and of the processes with W+X pages or a memfd file, which count processes too; modules the module count and its change; sockets the socket counts. Each group keeps the relations within it (a sum, a subset, the change of one quantity), so D breaks only the relations between groups (proposal 7.4); a column of class rule or dropped (G3a) is no TCN input and D leaves it as it is. An intervention is evaluable when it passes the validity predicate and at least analysis.evaluable.scored_share of its first analysis.evaluable.first_s seconds is scored (proposal 6.4); a class with fewer than min_evaluable evaluable interventions is nevyhodnotené (proposal 6.4, the lead's skeleton B7 section 5), and min_evaluable is analysis.min_occurrences (proposal 6.4 states one rule for a type or a class). K2 pools the two classes (the lead's skeleton B7 section 9: D is computed from every intervention of both classes; tcn/k2.py POOL_RULE): whenever at least one class is evaluated, the share of a method in a boot is the number of its evaluable interventions detected over every planned intervention of both classes in the boot, the volume class and the interventions not placed in the denominator and never a success, a class below the minimum included; such a class is reported nevyhodnotené by class, in the record of K2 and in its table by class and length (descriptive), and K2a and K2b are nevyhodnotené only when no class is evaluated. Z1's criterion on the interventions inserted into dev pools the classes alike (verification of B7b, F1).

diagnostics.note: Proposal 8.5 and the lead's skeleton B7 section 6, descriptive only (they decide neither K1 nor K2): the decision tree of depth at most tree_depth over the raw columns of the last row, their differences and the largest bin change, cross-validated by boots, and the share of one member, both also for Z1 to Z3, where they must come out threshold-like or the diagnostic is not used, and with fewer than min_positive_episodes positive episodes not evaluated; the context truncated to each length of contexts rows (31 is the full context of the window of 32 rows), for M and for Z3 and Z5; the alarm rules [k, n] of alarm_rules, analysis.alarm_rule among them; the model with shuffled context (the last row kept) and the network with random weights; the threshold from clean traffic only beside the main one (proposal 8.7) and the threshold with one boot of calibration left out; the partial models over the memory aggregates mem_* only, over the global part only and over the bin part only (the skeleton's addendum 2 point 3). The numbers are the lead's (skeleton section 6).

alarm_rate_interval.source: The thesis (the lead's skeleton dokazy/B7/kostra/KOSTRA.md, addendum 2 point 2: false alarms per hour of evaluated time with the exact two-sided Poisson interval of Garwood). The level 0.95 is the one tcn/eval.py has given the thesis' interval since iteration 1 (alfa 0.05, alfa/2 on each side) and the 95 % of proposal 8.4 and 9.2.

dispersion.source: The thesis (skeleton B7, addendum 2 point 2: a test whether the alarm counts differ between sessions more than chance gives): Pearson's X2 of the counts of the sessions against their expectation in proportion to the time of each, with sessions - 1 degrees of freedom, as tcn/eval.py has computed it since iteration 1 (judgment: the time is the observed time, the main denominator of proposal 4.2, where iteration 1 took the scored time). It has no number of its own: its p-value is reported.

event_vs_clean.source: The thesis (skeleton B7, addendum 2 point 2: the alarm rate during events against clean traffic on test_benign, a one-sided exact test of two Poisson rates at alpha 0.05, in total and per event type): the exact conditional test, the alarms during events among all the alarms of both against the binomial law of the share of the observed time the events hold, as tcn/eval.py porovnanie_mier has computed it since protocol v3 (NAVRH_PROTOKOL_V3 kap. 5). alpha 0.05 is the thesis'.

o2_bound.source: Proposal 4.2 row O2 (alarms per observed hour of clean traffic with an exact one-sided bound, per channel and in total) and 9.2, whose table is this bound: the one-sided upper bound of the Poisson mean, chi2.ppf(level, 2k + 2) / 2, over the clean observed hours (0 alarms in 16.8 hours give 0.18 per hour, 1 alarm 0.28). The level 0.95 is proposal 9.2's.

o3_bound.source: Proposal 4.2 row O3 (the share of evaluable occurrences with an alarm per event type, with a bound) and 9.2 (12 evaluable occurrences without an alarm give 0.22 as the upper bound of the probability of an alarm): the one-sided exact upper bound of Clopper and Pearson, beta.ppf(level, k + 1, n - k), 1 when every occurrence has an alarm. The level 0.95 is proposal 9.2's.

classifier.source: The thesis (skeleton B7, addendum 2 point 2: accuracy and macro-F1 over windows and the majority class per session and per occurrence) and proposal 4.2 row O6 (the majority vote per occurrence beside the most frequent class and chance).

metrics.note: Package B7c (design dokazy/B7/navrh/NAVRH_B7c.md 1.2 and 1.3): the metrics as the thesis defines them (the lead's skeleton B7, addendum 2 point 2), which tcn/eval.py computes beside the proposal's from the replays, per channel of the detector (rule, neural, kernel_integrity) and for their union; descriptive, they decide neither K1 nor K2. alarm_rate_interval is the interval of the alarms per observed hour of every evaluated row of a role (on test_benign every alarm is false: the events are part of normal, D10), dispersion the test of their counts over its sessions, event_vs_clean the test of the rate during the events against the rate in clean traffic, o2_bound the bound of O2 and o3_bound the bound of O3 (proposal 4.2 and 9.2), classifier the measures of the activity classifier (a bundle without classes, a baseline of tcn/porovnanie.py, has none). Each metric names its source; method is the one tcn/eval.py implements (scripts/protocol_v5.py METRIC_METHODS).

linkage.VO2: O2, O3 a test z bodu 2 (E2)
linkage.VO3: časť vlastníka so vzorkami, mimo protokolu (E3, D16)
linkage.note: The table of the lead's skeleton dokazy/B7/kostra/KOSTRA.md, addendum 2 point 4 (2026-11-22T20:55Z), word for word: each research question of chapter 3 of the thesis (VO1 to VO6) with the outputs of this protocol that answer it and, in parentheses, the experiment of the thesis (E1 to E5). 'bod 1' is point 1 of that addendum (the comparison models of the thesis in the core, analysis.descriptive_methods), 'bod 2' its point 2 (the metrics as the thesis defines them, analysis.metrics) and 'test z bodu 2' the one-sided exact test of the alarm rate during events against clean traffic of that point (analysis.metrics.event_vs_clean); VO3 is the owner's part with malware samples, outside this protocol (decision D16: tcn.eval malver). The record of the final command and the pre-registration document carry the table (design B7c 1.2 and 1.4); scripts/protocol_v5.py LINKAGE holds the same table and the self-check compares them.

attachments.series: The series of score, threshold and alarms per row (the lead's answer to question Q17, 2026-11-24): for every session of the test roles test_benign and test_controls, every method of the final evaluation (M at every seed of analysis.seeds, Z0 to Z5 with both variants of Z4, the descriptive methods at their seeds) and every row of the session by its seq and time: the score of the window that ends at the row (NaN where none ends there), whether it exceeds the method's matched threshold (one number per method), whether the alarm k of n is up and whether an alarm begins there (tcn/metody.py ALARM_RULE), and whether that window is clean traffic (CLEAN_RULE); M also by its replays at the bundle threshold with every channel of each row (safeguard replay: its score, the alarm of each channel, the alarm, its rising edge and its sources); and the host times of every event and control of those sessions, with its type or kind, its polarity and whether it ran.
attachments.losses: The losses per window of the predictors (the lead's answer to question Q28, 2026-11-24): M at every seed of analysis.seeds, Z3, Z5 and the GRU and LSTM predictors at their seeds, the loss of tcn/metody.py LOSS_FORMULA (the training loss) of the window that ends at each row of every session of the test roles, by seq and time (NaN where no window ends there), with whether that window is clean traffic: K1 and the losses of the record take the clean windows of test_benign.
attachments.copies: The series of the copies of the interventions that K2 detects (the lead's answer to question Q28, 2026-11-24): every placed intervention of test_benign and test_controls (its id, class, length, order or group, boot, session, start and status), and every row of its copy by seq and time: whether it lies in the block, whether the window that ends there lies in the horizon of tcn/k2.py DETECTION_RULE, and for every method and seed of K2 at its matched threshold the score of that window (NaN where none ends there), whether it exceeds, whether the alarm k of n is up and whether an alarm begins there.
attachments.note: Proposal 10.8 and the lead's answers to questions Q17 and Q28 (2026-11-24): the final record carries these three attachments and no other, a list written in G0 before any data; a figure drawn from an attachment is not a new reading of a test role (Q17), and a later need of anything else from the test roles is a deviation of chapter 11.3, which the owner decides. Each attachment is one file beside the record, <record stem>.<name>.npz (numpy savez_compressed: float64 exact, read by numpy.load with allow_pickle=False; the executor's format), named in values.attachments of the record by its path, sha256, bytes, format, contents and rule (tcn/finalne.py ATTACHMENT_RULE); a failed record names none. Not attached (judgment): the random variant of Z0, drawn per window set from the stream z0_alarms (its record gives the seeds and the mean rates), and the networks of the diagnostics, which are no methods of the comparison.

analysis.note: The analysis plan of proposal 10.1 point 3 (chapters 6.4, 7.4, 8.3, 8.4): the model enters K1 and K2 by its median over the five seeds, the deployed bundle is seed 0 (D14); fpr 0.01 and the rule 3 of 5 are kept (chapter 12); K1 against the prediction methods, K2a against the threshold methods, K2b against the methods with time and no learning; an occurrence is evaluable when at least half of its first 60 s is scored; a type or class with fewer than 8 evaluable occurrences is not evaluated. The bounds m are set in G1, the grids and the classes of the columns (analysis.columns) in G3a. The numbers of the G0 rows are the author's judgment by proposal 10.9. Package B7a (the lead's skeleton dokazy/B7/kostra/KOSTRA.md sections 2 to 4 and its addendum 2 point 1): Z0, Z2, Z4 and M have no free parameter (grid {}), only the grids of Z1, Z3 and Z5 wait for G3a; descriptive_methods are the z-score, the isolation forest and the GRU and LSTM predictors in the same wrapper as Z0 to Z5 (M's windows and normalizer, the behaviour inputs with the bin summary of tcn/baselines.py zluc_biny, a threshold at the matched alarm rate), reported beside M and Z (the loss of the predictors, the share of interventions detected, the alarms per hour) and deciding neither K1 nor K2; wording holds the conclusions of chapter 8.4 word for word (the text inside its quotation marks, the blanks where the table has them); matched_rate and statistics hold the rules of the matched alarm rate and of the interval and the test of K1 and K2. Package B7b (the lead's skeleton B7 sections 5, 6 and 9, design B7b 1.4): interventions holds the orders of C, the groups of D, the validity predicate, the evaluable minimum and the volume class, and diagnostics the bounds of the diagnostics of proposal 8.5. K2 pools the classes C and D (skeleton section 9): a class with fewer than 8 evaluable interventions is reported nevyhodnotené by class and stays in the pooled shares, and K2 is nevyhodnotené only when no class is evaluated (interventions.note). K2a compares the two variants of Z4 as two comparisons, Z4:load and Z4:residual, each with its own stream bootstrap, and 'better' needs M to beat both (the lead's answer to question Q13, 2026-11-24). Clean traffic, for the budget, the thresholds, the rates and K1, is the time outside the events and their reverberation (proposal 4.2; the lead's answer to question Q12, 2026-11-24): the full-snapshot band bounds only where the interventions are placed, and the rate is per observed hour of clean traffic. Package B7c (the lead's skeleton B7, addendum 2 points 2 and 4, design B7c 1.2): metrics holds the metrics as the thesis defines them and the bounds of O2 and O3 (proposal 4.2 and 9.2), each with its numbers and its source, and linkage the table of the thesis' research questions and the outputs that answer them, word for word; both are G0 and descriptive. Package B11 (the lead's answers of 2026-11-24): the validity predicate of the interventions judges a new deviation only (interventions.validity, question Q14), and attachments lists in advance the three attachments of the final record (series, losses and copies, questions Q17 and Q28); both are G0.

rehearsal.note: Proposal 10.4 and POKYNY 2026-11-22 section 4 (question 10): a rehearsal is a mode of this file, with its own name and group prefix and 2 groups per role (10 groups, 30 sessions, every role on every VM); its scenario counts differ by at most 1 over the whole plan (skeleton section 6).
